Fixture: 08_modular_gray16_32x32_lossless.jxl
32x32 grayscale, 16-bit samples, mathematically lossless

Purpose
-------
Targets slices 5/6/7 (modular decoding, frame headers, end-to-end lossless).
Exercises the >8-bit sample path through modular: source is a PGM with
maxval 65535 (two big-endian bytes per sample per the PNM spec), so the
bitstream must carry a bit_depth signaling 16, and the modular buffer/tree
predictor arithmetic must operate correctly at full 16-bit range rather than
assuming 8-bit samples clamp everything.

Interesting side effect: unlike every other fixture in this batch, cjxl
wrapped this stream in the ISOBMFF-style box container (00 00 00 0c 4a 58 4c
20 ... `ftyp` ... `jxll` ... `jxlc`) rather than emitting a naked FF 0A
codestream. This looks like it is driven by the >8-bit depth, not by size or
any flag we passed -- worth a decoder test on its own once box parsing is
exercised, since 01_signature_container.bin only covers the *signature*, not
a real decodable container stream. Confirmed by hex inspection, not by
reading libjxl source.

Provenance
----------
  Encoder:      cjxl v0.13.0 196a43d9 [_AVX2_,SSE4,SSE2] {GNU 15.2.0}
  libjxl rev:   196a43d996aa6ed33ebf98812a7c6d43b2b6d01b (v0.12-snapshot-2-g196a43d9)
  cjxl flags:   -d 0 -e 3
  Built by:     tools/setup-oracles.sh (flags recorded in
                tools/oracle-bin/PINNED_REVISIONS.txt)
  Regenerate:   tools/make-modular-fixtures.sh
                That script IS the recipe; it rewrites the source and re-encodes.

  Source image: tests/fixtures/generated/src_gray16_32x32.pgm  (2063 bytes)
                sha256 ccea9d8f796f91585994a804d36f72e5ca57af048e4105cc7eef0f56d5b7b32d
                Synthetic, written by the Python snippet inside
                tools/make-modular-fixtures.sh -- no third-party image was
                used, converted, or consulted. 32x32 16-bit grayscale (PGM
                P5, maxval 65535):
                  v(x, y) = (x + y) * 65535 / 62      diagonal ramp, 0..65535
                Same diagonal-ramp shape as 07, scaled to the full 16-bit
                range so the fixture actually needs 16 bits (a ramp that
                tops out under 256 would be indistinguishable from an 8-bit
                stream at the sample-value level).

  Fixture:      242 bytes
                sha256 8cbf9e10108971326d3b090e478ab2bf26e7e0019682a46361226c831b38f3e1

Verification
------------
djxl decodes it to a PGM byte-identical to the source, including both bytes
of every 16-bit sample (checked on every run of
tools/make-modular-fixtures.sh -- a `cmp -s` over the full PGM, so a
byte-order or truncation bug would fail this). Classified by `jpxl info`
(jpxl-cli) as a recognized "container" stream.

Modular features engaged
-------------------------
Not independently confirmed beyond ">8-bit signaling forces the box
container" (observed, not read from source) and "Modular, lossless" as
printed by cjxl at encode time. jxlinfo is not built in this checkout; djxl
-v / -v -v print no per-feature detail for this stream either. See
07_modular_gray_8x8_lossless.jxl.txt for the general caveat on
feature-introspection limits with this oracle.

cjxl is used strictly as a BLACK BOX: it emits conformant streams for JPXL to
parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a different libjxl
revision changes these digests, that is the point of recording them -- do not
silently update them; note the revision change.
